description: Multi-phase plans currently in flight. Each phase references roadmap item ids; the activePhase section breaks the current phase into concrete tasks with status. Survives conversation compactions — a fresh session can pick up by reading this file.

phases.title: Foundation
phases.notes: Schema, bus, episodic memory, agent base. Nothing alive yet — just the substrate everything else hangs off.

phases.title: First Voice
phases.notes: Cheshire Cat end-to-end. Talking to himself. Layered context composer + engagement policy + ADR writer come online here because the Cat is their first consumer.

phases.title: First Tension
phases.notes: Add the White Rabbit. Two voices, role tension, semantic + relational memory layers populated as the agents accumulate history. Compaction-as-behavior arrives because it has to.

phases.title: First Race
phases.notes: Dodo orchestrator + quiescence + conflict resolution + first showcase (/health endpoint). The system runs end-to-end on a trivial directive. Init CLI lands here so the showcase can run against a real target project.

phases.title: Full Cast
phases.notes: Bring the rest of the cast online with integration tests per agent. Per-character artifact handlers for the new speech act payloads. Synthetic-consensus guard goes here because it only matters once disagreement is real.

phases.title: Real Threads
phases.notes: The hard showcases — translation chat MVP, security recovery, multi-session persistence. Transcript annotation tooling lets us publish them. Token telemetry confirms the engagement_policy is paying for itself. Closed out 2026-05-08; substrate-convergence work in analyses 026-030 + the Geocities showcase landed the "Tweedles don't ship" bug class. P7 evals deferred behind P8 (operator interface) so the eval harness has a usable surface to run against.

phases.title: Observer API
phases.notes: HistoricalRunHandle reads any captured snapshot directory — parses run.log, reads the per-agent SQLite databases, loads the telemetry JSON, exposes summary() / meetings() / utterances() / per_agent_telemetry() / artifacts(). The replay-side surface that everything else in P8 sits on. Shipped 2026-05-07 alongside P8.2.

phases.title: TUI Inspector
phases.notes: Textual-based read-only TUI: snapshot library, run summary, meeting detail with body preview + speaker filter + utterance modal, artifact browser (global + meeting-scoped, attribution via bus not mtime), cast view, theme cycling, app-wide vim navigation. First public release — wonderland-ai 0.0.1 on PyPI 2026-05-08.

phases.title: Streaming + Mock Turtle
phases.notes: Foundation for live-watch UX. Extend RunHandle with stream_events() async iterator; HistoricalRunHandle defaults to yield-now (no behavior change for inspector); MockTurtleHandle replays a snapshot's events with compressed timing + dwell cap so we iterate live-watch UI against a free testbed. After P8.3 the TUI can subscribe to "events as they arrive" without caring whether the source is replay, mock, or eventually a real bus.

phases.title: Live-watch screen
phases.notes: New LiveRunScreen that consumes the streaming API — meeting cells fill in as events arrive, current speaker indicator, live cost ticker, drill-down into in-progress meetings shows partial transcripts. Iterated entirely against Mock Turtle replay so zero API spend during UX iteration. The screen that turns Wonderland from "things happen and you read transcripts later" into "things happen and you watch them happen."

phases.title: Directive issuing + LiveRunHandle
phases.notes: NewRunScreen — directive textarea, workflow picker (TDD/canonical/smoke), project-root picker. LiveRunHandle wraps a real Runner+Caucus, emits via the same streaming API as MockTurtleHandle so the live-watch screen consumes both interchangeably. The leap from "replay testbed" to "actually launches a real run." First end-to-end test: directive → live watch → artifacts → done.

phases.title: New-project spinup (the rabbit hole)
phases.notes: Three entry paths converging on a single project-context capture: greenfield (skeleton picker + scaffold), existing-Wonderland (already covered by P8.5's project picker), adopt-existing (wonderland init + stack-detection routine that pre-fills the context form from manifest files). Persists .wonderland/project-context.md in a forward-compatible shape so future workflow-context injection has one input format to read. The on-ramp that turns "pip install" into "team's ready to start."

phases.title: First-use polish
phases.notes: Welcome/home screen (new run / browse snapshots / cast / configure), error states (missing API key, no project root, run failure), abort flow (clean shutdown of running threads), quiescence indicator (M5's long pauses need "still working, just thinking"), README + SHOWCASE updates with the TUI flow. The rough-edges sweep that closes the gap between "works for the developer" and "works for someone who just installed it."

phases.title: Evals
phases.notes: Generic-baseline vs Wonderland comparison. The compounding-curve plot is the legibility-of-value mitigation from §11. Without this the philosophy stays assertion.

activePhase.title: Live-watch screen
activePhase.goal: Build the TUI live-watch screen against MockTurtleHandle. Per analysis 032 + the P8.3 work that just closed: the streaming foundation exists, MockTurtle provides snapshot replay at clock time without API spend, and the consumer-side ergonomics work inside Textual's runtime (verified by T44). P8.4 builds the LiveRunScreen on top of that — meeting cells fill in as events arrive, current speaker indicator updates per UtteranceEmitted, live cost ticker accumulates from AgentTelemetryDelta events. Drill-down into in-progress meetings shows partial transcripts. Iterated entirely against Mock Turtle replay. After P8.4: pivot to P8.5 (directive issuing + LiveRunHandle) for the leap to real runs.
activePhase.sequencing: Layout first, before behavior. The screen has three primary regions: a meetings ribbon (one cell per meeting, filling in as MeetingStarted/Ended events fire), a transcript pane (the active meeting's utterances scrolling in real-time), and a status bar (current speaker, live cost, time elapsed). Iteration cadence: layout sketch + minimal data flow → drill-into-meeting on click/Enter → cost ticker → speaker indicator → polish. Each iteration ships against the v6 banner (parallel TDD, no per_item) AND v3 (tdd-serial, 11 per_item iterations) so per_item handling is exercised throughout. Per_item iteration metadata on MeetingStarted/Ended is currently None (roadmap 7a5ff815 fixes the meetings() parser); design the UI so it degrades gracefully when iteration_label is missing — show base meeting label with a discriminator from thread_id slug suffix until that lands.

tasks.title: LiveRunScreen layout — three-region skeleton
tasks.details:
First task in P8.4. Build the LiveRunScreen layout in src/wonderland/tui/screens/live_run.py with three primary regions:

  - **Meetings ribbon** (top): one cell per meeting, fills in as MeetingStarted/MeetingEnded events fire. Each cell shows the meeting label (M1, M2, etc.) + a status indicator (pending / in-progress / complete / over-budget). Per_item iterations get their own cells.

  - **Transcript pane** (middle, takes most of the screen): the active meeting's utterances scrolling in real-time as UtteranceEmitted events arrive. Format mirrors the existing meeting-detail transcript: time, speaker, act, body preview.

  - **Status bar** (bottom): current speaker, live cost ticker, time elapsed. Empty/dashed values until events arrive.

T45 scope is *layout only* — renders static dummy data (a hand-built list of fake meetings + utterances). No streaming wire yet; that's T46. The layout has to look right before we make it live.

Acceptance:
  - LiveRunScreen class instantiates and renders without crashing.
  - Three regions are visually distinct (style hints from the existing wonderland.tcss).
  - Vim navigation routes correctly (j/k cycles meeting cells in the ribbon).
  - Test in test_tui_smoke.py asserts the screen mounts cleanly with a hand-built RunEvent list.
tasks.resolution:
T45 ships LiveRunScreen layout in src/wonderland/tui/screens/live_run.py — three regions visible:

  1. Meetings ribbon (top, ~30% screen height): a DataTable with columns for Meeting / Status / Calls / Cost. Status icons: · pending, ⟳ in-progress, ✓ complete, ⚠ over-budget. One row per meeting; per_item iterations get their own rows.

  2. Transcript pane (middle, takes 1fr remaining space): a RichLog widget that streams utterance rows in real-time. Format: '+12.3s alice story → body preview' with speaker name highlighted in cyan and speech act in yellow.

  3. Status bar (bottom, single line): current speaker / live cost / elapsed time. Renders 'idle' / dashes when no events seen yet.

Layout-only; renders against hand-built dummy data (3 meetings, 3 utterances, fixed cost+speaker). T46 wires the actual MockTurtleHandle.stream_events() consumption into on_mount.

Includes _label_from_thread_id helper for synthesizing per_item iteration discriminators when iteration_label is None on streaming events (graceful degradation pending roadmap 7a5ff815). Takes (meeting_label, thread_id, base_meeting_id) — base id has to be passed by caller because base ids may themselves contain hyphens (test-scenarios, contract-negotiation), so prefix-matching from thread_id alone isn't reliable.

Tests (tests/test_tui_smoke.py, +6):
  - TestLabelFromThreadId: 4 cases — base = thread_id, iteration synthesis, simple base id, unknown prefix fallback
  - test_live_run_screen_mounts_with_dummy_data: 3-meeting ribbon, 3-utterance log, populated status bar state
  - test_live_run_screen_vim_navigation_works: j/k move cursor in the meetings table

35 TUI smoke tests pass total. CSS hooks added to wonderland.tcss (live-header, transcript-log, live-status, etc.).

T46 next: replace _render_static_dummy with a streaming subscription to MockTurtleHandle, populate ribbon + transcript + status bar from real event flow.

tasks.title: Wire MockTurtle stream consumption to LiveRunScreen
tasks.details:
T45's layout becomes live. The screen subscribes to a RunHandle's stream_events() async iterator and updates state as events arrive:

  - MeetingStarted: insert a new cell in the meetings ribbon (or update an existing cell from pending → in-progress).
  - UtteranceEmitted: append a row to the transcript pane.
  - ArtifactShipped: render an inline artifact pill in the transcript row that emitted it.
  - MeetingEnded: update the cell's status (complete / over-budget per outcome).
  - AgentTelemetryDelta: update status bar cost ticker.
  - RunStarted/RunEnded: bookend status messages.

Per_item degradation: when iteration_label is None (current state per roadmap 7a5ff815), derive a discriminator from the thread_id slug suffix (e.g., 'test-scenarios-focus-session-with-visual-countdown' → 'Focus Session With Visual Countdown' as a synthesized label). UI degrades gracefully even before that fix lands.

Stream consumption pattern: launch as a worker via Textual's @work decorator (or asyncio.create_task within on_mount) so the main UI thread stays responsive. Per T44's interleaving test, the async iterator pattern is non-blocking already — just need to integrate cleanly with Textual's event/worker model.

Iterate against both v6 banner (parallel TDD, no per_item) and v3 (tdd-serial, 11 per_item iterations) so both cases are exercised.

Acceptance:
  - Open LiveRunScreen with a MockTurtleHandle for v6 banner; meeting cells fill in correctly (7 cells, all complete after stream drains).
  - Open with v3 snapshot; 11 cells fill in (M4×3 + M5×3 visible as distinct cells with discriminators).
  - Transcript scrolls as utterances arrive.
  - No deadlock or starved event loop (pilot.press still responsive during stream).
  - Tests in test_tui_smoke.py.
tasks.resolution:
T46 wires MockTurtleHandle.stream_events() into LiveRunScreen via Textual's @work decorator.

on_mount branches: if snapshot_dir is set, kick off the @work-decorated _consume_stream worker; otherwise fall back to T45's hand-built dummy data (preserves layout testing in isolation). The worker creates a MockTurtleHandle with the screen's speed + max_dwell_seconds, caches base meeting ids from handle.meetings(), then async-iterates stream_events() dispatching each event to a small handler.

Event handlers:
  - RunStarted: render header with workflow name + truncated directive
  - MeetingStarted: insert/update ribbon row; compose display label combining label, name, iteration metadata, and per_item discriminator (slug-derived when iteration_label is None)
  - UtteranceEmitted: append a transcript line with elapsed timestamp + speaker (cyan) + speech act (yellow) + body preview, update _current_speaker
  - ArtifactShipped: append an indented '↳ kind: title' line under the carrying utterance
  - AgentTelemetryDelta: track per-agent cost in a dict; recompute _total_cost as the sum (overwrites cleanly for live runs that fire deltas multiple times per agent)
  - MeetingEnded: update ribbon row's status (COMPLETE → complete; MEETING_BUDGET / GLOBAL_BUDGET / TIMEOUT / ABORTED → over-budget)
  - RunEnded: append closing transcript marker

Per_item iteration handling: _compose_meeting_label finds the base meeting id by prefix-matching against the cached list, derives the discriminator from iteration_label (preferred) or the slug suffix (fallback). Iteration count badge ('(2/3)') prepended when iteration_index/total are populated. v3 snapshot smoke confirms 11 ribbon rows with distinct labels for the 6 per_item iterations.

End-to-end smoke against v3 banner: 11 meetings rendered, total cost $4.7236 matches actual, M6 correctly marked over-budget (MEETING_BUDGET outcome), 242 transcript lines, last speaker = Dodo's closing acknowledgment.

Tests (+3 in tests/test_tui_smoke.py with a _drain_live_run_screen helper):
  - test_live_run_screen_streams_v6_banner: 7 ribbon rows, all in terminal status, cost > 0
  - test_live_run_screen_streams_v3_per_item_snapshot: 11 ribbon rows, 3 distinct M4 iterations + 3 distinct M5 iterations, distinct labels
  - test_live_run_screen_transcript_populated_after_stream: log line count >= utterance count

Suite runtime: 0.42-0.48s per T46 test (speed=1e6 + dwell=0 strips timing). 38 TUI smoke tests pass total.

Known limitation: MeetingEnded.cost_delta is always 0 from HistoricalRunHandle's stream_events (T41 didn't parse it from run.log END markers); per-meeting cost column shows $0.0000 even though the total is correct from AgentTelemetryDelta. T47 (next) is a natural place to fix that, or it can be a follow-on roadmap item.

tasks.title: Live status bar — current speaker, cost ticker, elapsed time
tasks.details:
The status bar at the bottom of LiveRunScreen accumulates per-event signals:

  - **Current speaker**: updates per UtteranceEmitted to show 'speaking: <agent_name>' for the most recent utterance. Renders 'idle' when no recent utterance (e.g., between meeting boundaries).

  - **Live cost ticker**: '\$X.YY' running total. Computed from AgentTelemetryDelta events (which fire once per agent at the end in HistoricalRunHandle, so for replay the ticker jumps at the end). Could optionally also accumulate from utterance events (tally per-agent calls and apply rough per-call estimate) to get a smoother feel during replay; defer to follow-on if it adds scope.

  - **Time elapsed**: wall-clock time since the stream started, formatted as MM:SS. Shows source-run time deltas if useful (e.g., '+12.3s' since last event).

Acceptance:
  - Status bar updates as events arrive.
  - Final cost matches sum of AgentTelemetryDelta values.
  - Speaker indicator highlights the most recent utterer.
  - Tests in test_tui_smoke.py.
tasks.resolution:
T47 ships three live-status improvements + the cost-delta gap fix folded in.

1. **HistoricalRunHandle.stream_events() now populates MeetingEnded.cost_delta / calls_delta / outcome from the run.log's META END markers** (T47 fold-in per user request, was the known limitation noted at end of T46). Added _parse_end_markers() helper that pre-parses every END line in chronological order; each MeetingEnded event consumes the next marker matching its meeting label, so per_item iterations get their per-iteration cost rather than 0. Verified end-to-end against v3 banner: every per-meeting cost column matches the run.log exactly (M1 \$0.0328, M2 \$0.0442, ..., M6 \$1.2007 = total \$4.7236).

2. **Live cost ticker** now accumulates from each MeetingEnded as it arrives (rather than jumping at the end when AgentTelemetryDelta finally fires). The status bar shows a smoothly climbing cost during replay. AgentTelemetryDelta still overwrites with the per-agent authoritative totals at the end — but until then the user sees cost increasing in real time as meetings complete.

3. **Wall-clock elapsed timer** in the status bar — distinct from source-time elapsed. The 'Watching: MM:SS' counter ticks via a 500ms set_interval refresh so it advances during quiet periods between events. The source-time 'Run time:' is shown alongside as a dim secondary indicator (handy for replay; tells the user where they are in the source run's own timeline).

Implementation:
  - historical.py: added _parse_end_markers helper + cursor-based marker consumption in stream_events
  - live_run.py: split _per_agent_cost (authoritative dict) from _meeting_cost_total (rolling estimate); status bar shows wall-clock + source-time; set_interval(0.5, _render_status_bar) added in on_mount

Tests (+1):
  - test_live_run_screen_per_meeting_costs_match_run_log: against v3 banner, every per-meeting cost matches the run.log; total matches the v3 \$4.7236 banner number

1348 tests pass full suite. 38 TUI smoke tests pass.

Two things didn't go in T47 that user explicitly raised but are roadmap-shaped, not directive-shaped:
  - Multi-pane lazygit-style detail view → folded into T48 (next task), retitled "Lazygit-style multi-pane drill-down with selection-driven filtering". User noted this as a primary UX influence; saved to project memory at memory/project_tui_lazygit_principle.md.
  - Call-by-call observer view → filed as roadmap d04fb3b3 (P1 feature). Composes with T48's lazygit panes naturally; would add a third 'Calls' pane showing every LLM call (not just bus emissions). Mostly surface-existing-data work (parse-error and late-publish events live in run.log already); the silent-call substrate gap is the deeper instrumentation piece.

tasks.title: Lazygit-style multi-pane drill-down with selection-driven filtering
tasks.details:
**lazygit-influenced redesign** (per user feedback after T46): instead of pushing a separate MeetingDetailScreen modal when the user selects a meeting cell, restructure the LiveRunScreen as a multi-pane layout where focus + selection drives filtering across adjacent panes.

Target layout (lazygit-style, no modals):

  ┌─ Run header ──────────────────────────────────────────┐
  ├─ Meetings (focusable) ─┬─ Transcript (filtered) ─────┤
  │ M1 [✓]                 │ +0.0s alice story → ...     │
  │ M2 [✓]                 │ +1.2s rabbit ticket → ...   │
  │ M3 [✓] ← selected      │ +3.4s rabbit ticket → ...   │
  │ M4-1 [⟳]               │                             │
  │ M4-2 [·]               │                             │
  │ ...                    ├─ Artifacts (in meeting) ────┤
  │                        │ • story-001-...md           │
  │                        │ • ticket-001-...md          │
  └────────────────────────┴─────────────────────────────┘
  [ Status: speaker | cost | elapsed ]

Behavior:
  - Tab cycles focus between Meetings → Transcript → Artifacts (lazygit pattern)
  - Meetings focus: j/k selects a cell; Transcript and Artifacts panes filter to that meeting
  - Transcript focus: j/k scrolls within the selected meeting's utterances; Enter expands one
  - Artifacts focus: j/k navigates the list; Enter opens markdown via ArtifactDetailScreen (existing)
  - Special 'All meetings' pseudo-row shows the unfiltered rolling transcript (current T46 behavior — useful for 'what's happening RIGHT NOW')
  - Mid-stream: drilling into an in-progress meeting keeps receiving live updates

Implementation order:
  1. Restructure compose() into Horizontal multi-pane layout
  2. Per-meeting transcript + artifact buffers populated as events arrive
  3. Tab focus cycling between panes
  4. Selection-driven filtering (meeting → transcript + artifacts)
  5. Enter on artifact → ArtifactDetailScreen (existing code reusable)

Acceptance:
  - Tab through panes works without modal screens
  - Selecting M2 shows M2's transcript + artifacts; selecting M4-iter-2 shows just that iteration
  - Mid-stream drill into in-progress meeting shows live updates
  - Enter on artifact opens its markdown
  - Tests in test_tui_smoke.py covering focus cycling, selection filtering, mid-stream drill
tasks.resolution:
T48 ships the lazygit-style multi-pane redesign. LiveRunScreen now has three focusable panes — Meetings (left), Transcript (top-right), Artifacts (bottom-right) — with selection in the Meetings pane driving filtering across the other two.

Layout (from compose()):

  ┌─ Header ──────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
  │ Run watch · workflow · directive                          │
  ├─ Meetings ─────────────┬─ Transcript ───────────────────────┤
  │ All meetings ← default │ +0.0s alice         story    → ...  │
  │ M1 — The Caucus Race   │ +1.2s rabbit        ticket   → ...  │
  │ M2 — Rabbit's Errand   │ ...                                 │
  │ M2.5 — Caterpillar     ├─ Artifacts ────────────────────────┤
  │ ... ← cursor changes   │ story-001-...md                     │
  │     filter             │ ticket-001-...md                    │
  │                        │ ...                                 │
  └────────────────────────┴────────────────────────────────────┘
  [ Status: speaker | cost | watching | run-time ]

Behavior:
  - 'All meetings' pseudo-row at index 0 = default; shows the unfiltered rolling stream (T46 behavior preserved as the natural default for live watching)
  - Cursor onto a specific meeting = transcript and artifacts panes filter to that meeting's content
  - Cursor on artifact row + Enter = ArtifactDetailScreen (existing markdown viewer)
  - Tab cycles focus between the three panes (Textual default — all three are focusable DataTable / RichLog widgets)
  - Mid-stream: as new events arrive for the selected meeting, they append-render to the visible panes; events for other meetings buffer silently and become visible if the user selects that meeting

Implementation:
  - compose() wraps Meetings + (Transcript + Artifacts) in a Horizontal split
  - Per-meeting buffers in __init__: _meeting_transcripts dict[thread_id, [(Utterance, ts)]] and _meeting_artifacts dict[thread_id, [RunArtifact]], with __all__ as sentinel for the unfiltered view
  - _last_open_thread_id tracks the most-recently-opened meeting so ArtifactShipped events attribute correctly (distinct from _selected_thread_id which is user-driven)
  - on_data_table_row_highlighted detects meetings-table cursor moves and triggers _refresh_panes_for_selection (clears + repopulates the transcript log and artifacts table)
  - _format_transcript_line factored out so the same formatting works whether streaming live or rebuilding from the buffer
  - _render_meetings_ribbon preserves cursor position across re-renders (the ribbon updates per MeetingStarted/Ended event, but the user shouldn't lose their selection)

Tests (+2 in tests/test_tui_smoke.py):
  - test_live_run_screen_filtering_by_meeting_selection: cursor on All-Meetings shows full stream; j moves cursor onto a specific meeting which becomes _selected_thread_id; transcript log re-renders with only that meeting's utterances; k back to All-Meetings restores
  - test_live_run_screen_artifacts_pane_populates: artifacts table count matches the filtered set for the selected meeting

Plus 3 existing tests updated to account for the +1 row in the meetings table (All-Meetings pseudo-row): v6 now reports 8 rows instead of 7, v3 reports 12 instead of 11, dummy data reports 4 instead of 3.

41 TUI smoke tests pass. 1350 tests pass full suite.

The lazygit principle from project memory (project_tui_lazygit_principle.md) is now manifest in the screen: focus + selection drives filtering across adjacent panes; no modals (except for ArtifactDetailScreen which earns its full-canvas use rendering markdown).

P8.4 closes — all five tasks done. Streaming foundation works, layout works, real events flow, costs match, lazygit filtering works, mid-stream drilling preserves the experience. The screen is ready to iterate on visually.

Next phase: P8.5 (Directive issuing + LiveRunHandle) is the leap to real runs. Same UI; live source.

tasks.title: Wire LiveRunScreen entry from snapshot library
tasks.details:
Add a 'watch in replay mode' entry path from the existing SnapshotLibraryScreen. Pressing 'w' on a snapshot row (or a button labeled '▶ Watch') opens LiveRunScreen wrapped around a MockTurtleHandle for that snapshot at default speed (5x, max_dwell=2s).

The existing 'Enter' on a snapshot row already opens the inspector view (RunSummaryScreen). 'w' becomes the alternative entry: same snapshot, different framing — replay-as-it-happened vs static inspection.

Optionally surface a speed selector before opening (a small modal: 1x / 5x / 10x / faithful original / smoke-test) so users can pick their pace. Defer to follow-on if it adds scope; default speed is fine for v1.

Acceptance:
  - 'w' on a snapshot row in the library opens LiveRunScreen.
  - Stream auto-starts on mount.
  - Escape returns to the library.
  - The keybinding shows in the library's footer for discoverability.
  - Test in test_tui_smoke.py.
